title: How to enlarge cursor in Chrome on Mac: a guide for better visibility
metaTitle: How to Enlarge Cursor in Chrome on Mac
description: Learn how to enlarge cursor in Chrome on Mac by adjusting system settings. Follow our simple guide to improve your browser navigation and accessibility.
intro: To enlarge the cursor in Chrome on your Mac, you must adjust the pointer settings in your macOS System Settings. Chrome does not have its own internal cursor size control, so changing the system-wide pointer size will apply to your browser automatically.
tldr: Open System Settings on your Mac.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to your preference.
Changes apply globally, including inside the Chrome browser.

blocks.text: Why Chrome does not have a cursor setting

Many users search for a way to change the mouse pointer size directly within the Chrome settings menu. You will not find this option because Google Chrome relies on the operating system to handle the cursor. This is a design choice that keeps the browser lightweight. When you modify the pointer, you are changing the Mac environment itself. This ensures that your cursor looks and acts the same way in every app, from Chrome to Mail or Pages.
Step by step to change your pointer size
Follow these steps to increase the visibility of your cursor.

items: Click the Apple Menu () in the top-left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Click the Accessibility tab in the left-hand sidebar.
Find the Pointer section on this page.
Slide the Pointer size slider to the right to make the cursor larger.
You can also adjust the pointer outline color and fill color here.

blocks.text: Using keyboard shortcuts for accessibility

If you need to change your accessibility settings often, you can use a keyboard shortcut to open the panel quickly. Pressing Command (⌘) + Option (⌥) + F5 will open the Accessibility Shortcuts panel. This allows you to toggle display features on or off without digging through the menu. This is particularly useful if you share your Mac with others who prefer a standard cursor size.
Troubleshooting cursor issues in Chrome

Sometimes the cursor might look wrong or fail to scale correctly when you move it over specific web elements. This is usually a minor rendering glitch in the Chromium engine. If you notice the cursor size does not update in Chrome, try refreshing the page. If that fails, restart the browser. This clears the temporary cache and forces Chrome to re-detect the current system pointer settings.
Managing cursor behavior on work devices

If you are using a Mac provided by your employer, you might find that the Accessibility settings are greyed out. This happens when your IT department uses device management software to lock certain settings. In this case, you will need to contact your system administrator. They can usually adjust these settings for you or grant you the necessary permissions to change your own accessibility preferences.
Improving web navigation with a larger pointer

A larger cursor is not just about visibility. It helps with precision. If you struggle to click small buttons or links, a larger pointer makes it easier to align your target. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines suggest that interactive elements should be at least 24x24 pixels. A larger cursor helps you hit these targets more accurately. This reduces the frustration of missing a button or clicking the wrong link on dense websites.
Customizing the pointer appearance

Beyond size, you can change the look of the pointer to make it stand out against different backgrounds. In the same Accessibility > Display panel, you can change the fill color and the outline color. A high-contrast color like bright yellow or white with a black outline is often easier to track on busy web pages. Experiment with these settings until you find a combination that works for your eyes.
The shake to locate feature

If you often lose track of where your cursor is, enable the Shake mouse pointer to locate setting. When this is on, a quick shake of your mouse or trackpad makes the cursor grow significantly for a second. This is perfect for users with large monitors or multiple screen setups. It provides an immediate visual cue that helps you find the pointer without searching the entire screen.
Why system-level changes are better

Some users look for Chrome extensions to change the cursor. We recommend against this. Extensions often slow down your browser and only work within the tab window. By using the macOS system settings, your cursor remains consistent everywhere. It stays large when you switch to other apps, when you are on your desktop, and when you are using system menus. This is the most reliable and efficient way to manage your pointer.
Staying updated with macOS and Chrome

Ensure your Mac is running a modern version of macOS. Chrome requires macOS 13 Ventura or later to receive the latest updates and security patches. Keeping your system updated ensures that accessibility features like the cursor scaling engine continue to work smoothly. If you are on an older version of macOS, you might miss out on performance improvements and better support for high-resolution displays.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor size only in Chrome?
faq.answer: No, macOS handles the cursor size globally. Any change you make in System Settings will affect your entire Mac, including Chrome.

faq.question: Why is my cursor size setting greyed out?
faq.answer: If the settings are greyed out, your Mac is likely managed by an IT department. You will need to ask an administrator to change the settings for you.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor size affect my browser performance?
faq.answer: No, increasing the cursor size has no impact on the performance or speed of Google Chrome.

faq.question: What is the best cursor color for visibility?
faq.answer: A bright fill color with a high-contrast outline, such as white with a black border, is typically the easiest to see on most web pages.

requirements: A Mac running macOS 13 or later

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner and select System Settings.

steps.name: Go to Accessibility
steps.text: Click on the Accessibility tab located in the left sidebar.

steps.name: Select Display
steps.text: Click the Display option to view pointer settings.

steps.name: Adjust Pointer Size
steps.text: Drag the Pointer size slider to your preferred level.
steps.tip: Move the slider slowly to find the size that feels most comfortable.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor size does not change in Chrome
troubleshooting.fix: Restart Chrome to allow the browser to refresh its pointer rendering.
Contact your IT administrator as your Mac may be managed by a company profile.
